subject: AuroraHealth private hosting connectivity snapshot & next asks
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: samira.khan@aurorahealth.com, aaron.lowe@aurorahealth.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AuroraHealth private hosting connectivity snapshot & next asks

Hi Samira / Aaron —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a short list of asks so we can prep the right tech folks for a follow-up deep dive. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update the notes.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Residency & compliance: Aurora must keep PHI within us-east-1 for prod, and research data needs an air-gapped/non-DNS environment for certain cohorts.
- Network constraints: minimum outbound egress (deny-by-default), IP allowlisting only to a small set of ranges, strict NAT/transit restrictions, and no public ingress to the enclave.
- Key mgmt: customer-managed KMS (FIPS/HSM) requirement for prod keys.
- Operational: separate non-prod vs prod onboarding timelines, and procurement/PO expected before prod testing.

Technical clarifications we need from your side
1) Can you share the non-prod network diagram (subnets, TGW/transit, NAT gateways) — helps us map peering vs private-link options.
2) For the air-gapped research environment: confirm whether DNS is fully disabled and whether you can provision an egress proxy for specific update URIs.
3) KMS/HSM: are you using Cloud HSM or a third-party appliance? Any specific compliance attestation text we should include?
4) Expected throughput and concurrency for the POC (tokens/sec, concurrent sessions) — we’ll size the environment accordingly.

Proposed next steps
- Tech deep dive (60min) to include Aurora infra and security; propose Fri 2pm or Mon 10am PT — please pick one or suggest alternatives.
- We’ll provide a focused VPC checklist and a short T-shirt sizing estimate for the POC ahead of the call (attached).
- You share the non-prod diagram; we’ll turn that into two recommended connectivity patterns (VPC peering with forced tunneling, or private hosted enclave with dedicated egress).

Attachments: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (short checklist we’ll use to align network asks)

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through these asks.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: samira.khan@aurorahealth.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: aaron.lowe@aurorahealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AuroraHealth private hosting connectivity snapshot & next asks

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few specifics to clarify on our end:
- Residency: Production must remain in us-east-1 (account 123456789012). Non-prod may live in a shared non-prod account but needs identical networking controls.
- Air-gap for research: DNS is disabled for the isolated research clusters. We can allow an outbound proxy to a small set of update URIs (listed in the attached diagram).
- IP ranges: we can provide /28 blocks for egress allowlisting per environment.
- KMS: we expect CloudHSM-backed keys with FIPS 140-2 level 3 assurance for prod.
- Procurement: our procurement timeline is ~6-8 weeks; we prefer a short POC (2 weeks) before moving to contract.

I attached our non-prod network diagram: aurora-nonprod-network-diagram_v2.pdf — it includes TGW and peering notes.

Samira Khan
Director, Infrastructure Security | AuroraHealth
samira.khan@aurorahealth.com | +1 202-555-0187

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: samira.khan@aurorahealth.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AuroraHealth private hosting connectivity snapshot & next asks

Samira — thanks for the diagram and the details. A few follow-ups and a proposed org for the tech deep dive so we can bring the right people.

Quick technical notes (based on attached diagram)
- Two connectivity patterns we recommend (we’ll sketch both in the deep dive):
  1) VPC peering + TGW -> forced-tunnel egress via a transit VPC (minimal changes to your infra; requires NAT/TGW ACL changes).
  2) Dedicated hosted enclave in customer account with private endpoints (no public internet egress by default); Redwood manages inference nodes but you maintain KMS/HSM and IGW restrictions.
- For the air-gapped clusters: if DNS is disabled, we need the proxy egress URIs and cert rotation plan. We can support pinned certs and static IP egress.
- KMS integration: CloudHSM is supported; we’ll need an IAM role and a short policy for key usage.

Can we schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive next week? I’m proposing:
- Tue Jul 6, 11:00am PT
- Wed Jul 7, 9:00am PT
Please pick one or share your availability. I’ll include our security engineer (Stephanie) and a runtime lead.

I’ve attached a short configuration proposal draft (redwood-configuration-proposal-draft.docx) — it’s high level but gives a sense of the integration points and required azure/iam/TGW changes.

On procurement sizing: if you can share expected concurrent sessions and tokens per minute for peak, we’ll produce a small/medium/large T-shirt sizing estimate before the deep dive.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0109

From: samira.khan@aurorahealth.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: aaron.lowe@aurorahealth.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AuroraHealth private hosting connectivity snapshot & next asks

Ben / Laura —

Appreciate the options — both look viable. We confirm the following and next steps:
- Include Aaron Lowe (CC’d) from procurement and infra security on the deep dive. Aaron will want a short written T-shirt sizing and an outline of required procurement items (SOW, PO line items).
- We can make Tue Jul 6, 11:00am PT work. Please send a calendar invite and include any pre-read (sizing + checklist).
- Attached is the svc-account-reqs.xlsx with our required service account and IAM patterns. Please review and call out any gaps.
- Our target: POC kickoff in ~4 weeks after preliminary sizing and contract discussions.

Two minor clarifications:
1) For the air-gapped research clusters we cannot use any 3rd-party telemetry that phones home; logs must be pushed to a local collector you can reach via a dedicated VPC endpoint.
2) Rotation windows for keys are 90 days; would need automation hooks for rotation events.

I’ll look out for the invite.

Samira
